question:
(i) Explain the meaning of unpolarised light and plane polarised light.
(ii) How does a polaroid convert unpolarised light into plane polarised light?
(iii) If unpolarised light of intensity $I_0$ is passed through a polaroid, find the transmitted intensity.

options.A:
(i) Unpolarised light has electric field vibrations only in one plane, while plane polarised light has vibrations in all directions.
(ii) A polaroid adds perpendicular vibrations.
(iii) The transmitted intensity is $I_0$.
options.B:
(i) Unpolarised and plane polarised light differ only in wavelength.
(ii) A polaroid changes the frequency of the incident light.
(iii) The transmitted intensity is $2I_0$.
options.C:
(i) In unpolarised light, electric-field vibrations occur in all possible directions perpendicular to propagation; in plane polarised light, they are confined to one plane.
(ii) A polaroid transmits only the vibration component parallel to its pass axis and absorbs the perpendicular components, producing plane polarised light.
(iii) For unpolarised incident light, the mean transmitted intensity is $I=\dfrac{I_0}{2}$.
options.D:
(i) Plane polarised light vibrates along the direction of propagation.
(ii) A polaroid converts it to longitudinal light.
(iii) The transmitted intensity is $I_0/4$.
